summary: dashboardContribution lineage backfill + durable-absence orphan sweep (cinatra#1628, S11a — the recovery floor for re-homing extension-shipped dashboards off the removed workflow kind, #1035). The five new dashboards columns (contribution_id, applied_contribution_version, applied_default_json, applied_default_hash, archive_reason), the contribution-id lookup index, and the two-tier partial UNIQUE indexes (dashboards_contribution_template_uniq on (contribution_id, organization_id) WHERE is_template; dashboards_contribution_instance_uniq on (contribution_id, organization_id, project_id) WHERE project_id NOT NULL) are ADDITIVE and land in the bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts); this migration owns the two TRANSFORMATIONAL data steps. (1) LEGACY→LINEAGE BACKFILL: every extension-owned row (extension_id NOT NULL) missing a contribution_id gets the deterministic carrier-independent lineage id 'legacy:<extension_id>', so a template + its per-project instances (which share extension_id) share one contribution_id; idempotent (contribution_id IS NULL guard) and 1:1 with the already-unique (extension_id, org[, project]) shape so it cannot violate the new partial UNIQUE indexes. (2) DURABLE-ABSENCE ORPHAN SWEEP: archive every non-archived extension-owned row whose package has NO installed_extension row at all (durable absence; a merely archived/disabled-but-present install is recoverable and left alone), stamping archive_reason='orphaned_contribution_sweep'; this is the data-hygiene companion to the all-reader liveness/status gate (the real fail-safe), safe because that gate also denies archived + non-live rows at read time. Gate class destructive: the same PR adds two partial UNIQUE indexes on the existing dashboards table (the gate's unique-index-on-existing-table rule) plus two UPDATE data rewrites, even though the partial indexes cover zero existing rows at creation (contribution_id is a brand-new all-NULL column) and the backfill is 1:1. Boot order guarantees safety: the bootstrap runs BEFORE core migrations, so the unique indexes already exist + enforce when the backfill commits; a fresh schema is ledger-faked and the table is empty. down() is a NO-OP (a backfilled contribution_id is indistinguishable from a reconcile-set one, and un-archiving swept rows would resurrect the orphan-render leak; the ledger records the run). SEQ: assigned at merge; shipped max is 0049 and #1674 holds 0050 — renumber to the next free seq if 0051 is taken before this merges.
